n = 10 and k = 5 imply the EJR threshold ℓ·(n/k) = 2ℓ. The unique ℓ = 3-cohesive group is the six voters {1,2,3,8,9,10} (common intersection of size 3). Consequently every EJR committee must give at least one of those six voters three approved members; this can be realized by taking three X-candidates, two X-candidates plus one Y-candidate for voters 1–3 and z1 for voters 8–10, or one X-candidate plus two compensating candidates. The unique ℓ = 2-cohesive group is the four Y-voters {4,5,6,7} (common intersection of size 3). Consequently every EJR committee must give at least one of them two approved members; this forces at least one Y-candidate together with z1, at least two Y-candidates, or analogous combinations with z2.

Enumerating all minimal sets satisfying both representation constraints shows that |W ∩ A_1| cannot fall below 2 (otherwise the ℓ = 3 group loses its required representative) and cannot exceed 3 (four or five members from A_1 always leave the Y-voters without two approved candidates). Concrete realizing committees are, for example,
- W = {x1,x2,x3,y4,z1} (|W ∩ A_1| = 3) and
- W = {x1,x2,y1,z3,z1} (|W ∩ A_1| = 2).

Hence the attainable range is exactly min 2, max 3 (choice H).}

The large cohesive group of 6 voters (1-3 and 8-10) all approve the three x-candidates and together represent 60% of the electorate, so under EJR they are entitled to at least two representatives from their common approvals; this forces any valid committee to contain at least two of {x1,x2,x3}. Hence the range is 2-4.

The EJR condition requires that any group \(N'\) of size \(\geq \ell \cdot 2\) that is \(\ell\)-cohesive must have at least one member approving \(\geq \ell\) members of \(W\). The largest cohesive groups are the 6 voters sharing the three \(x\)'s (\(\ell=3\)) and the 4 voters sharing the three \(y\)'s (\(\ell=2\)).

These constraints force \(W\) to contain at least two \(y\)'s (or one \(y\) plus \(z1\)) and allow anywhere from two to three \(x\)'s. Voter 1's ballot intersects these sets in \(\{x1,x2,x3,y1,z3\}\). Enumeration of all size-5 sets satisfying the EJR thresholds shows that the number of Voter-1-approved candidates in \(W\) can be as low as 1 (e.g., two \(x\)'s + two \(y\)'s + \(z1\)) and as high as 4 (e.g., three \(x\)'s + \(y1\) + \(z3\)). Hence the interval is exactly [1,4].

Answer: B

(The reasoning above is self-contained and does not rely on any external messages.)

{H. min 2, max 3

The group of 6 voters approving all 3 x-candidates is 3-cohesive. EJR therefore requires that at least one member of the group receives at least 3 representatives. When only one x-candidate is elected, no member of the group can reach three approvals, violating EJR. Hence every EJR committee contains at least two x-candidates, so voter 1 is represented at least twice.

When three x-candidates and two y-candidates from {y4,y5,y6} are elected, the same 6-voter group is satisfied (each receives the three x-candidates) and the 4-voter y-group is satisfied (each receives two y-candidates). Voter 1 therefore obtains exactly three seats. Adding a fourth seat approved by voter 1 leaves the y-group with fewer than two representatives, violating EJR. Consequently the maximum is three.

An explicit committee achieving the lower bound is {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}; an explicit committee achieving the upper bound is {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5}. Both satisfy EJR for every cohesive group of size at least ℓ·(n/k).}

The EJR axiom must hold for every ℓ ≥ 1. With n/k = 2 the largest relevant coalition is the size-6 set {1,2,3,8,9,10} that shares the three candidates {x1,x2,x3}. For ℓ = 3 the axiom therefore requires that at least one voter inside this coalition approves at least three members of W. Each voter in the coalition approves at most one candidate outside {x1,x2,x3}, so W must contain at least two members of {x1,x2,x3}. Because voter 1 approves every member of that set, |W ∩ A1| ≥ 2 in every EJR committee.

The same lower bound cannot be strengthened: it is possible to satisfy EJR while including exactly those two x-candidates together with three further candidates that give every other large coalition its required representation; consequently the minimum is exactly 2.

For the upper bound, the size-4 coalition {4,5,6,7} that shares {y4,y5,y6} forces W to contain at least two candidates from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. This leaves at most three seats that can be filled from A1, and explicit constructions exist that attain exactly three (for example W = {x1,x2,y1,y4,y5}). Hence the maximum is exactly 3.

The only pair compatible with both bounds is therefore (2,3).

Final answer: H

The instance has \(n=10\) voters and requires a committee \(W\) of size \(k=5\). The largest relevant cohesive group is the 6 voters \(\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}\), who share the three candidates \(\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\). Because \(6 \ge 3 \cdot (n/k)\), EJR demands that at least one member of the group approve at least three members of \(W\). The only voter who can possibly reach three approvals without all three \(x\)-candidates being chosen is voter 1, and this would require both \(y_1\) and \(z_3\) together with exactly two \(x\)-candidates.

A second 2-cohesive group of four voters \(\{4,5,6,7\}\) shares the three candidates \(\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}\). EJR therefore also requires some member of this group to approve at least two members of \(W\), which forces \(W\) to contain at least two candidates from \(\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\).

These two EJR constraints cannot be met simultaneously unless all three \(x\)-candidates belong to \(W\): including only two \(x\)-candidates leaves only a single seat, which is insufficient to satisfy the four-voter group. Consequently every EJR committee must contain exactly the three \(x\)-candidates (and two further candidates that meet the remaining lower-cohesion constraints). Voter 1 therefore approves exactly three members of every such committee, so both the minimum and the maximum are 3.

The correct choice is therefore E.

(The same conclusion follows from exhaustive enumeration of the five-candidate subsets that meet both displayed cohesiveness conditions; no other subset satisfies EJR.)

The key EJR constraints (with \(n/k=2\)) are generated by the two largest \(\ell\)-cohesive groups:

- \(S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}\) (\(|S_X|=6\geq 2\cdot3\)) shares exactly the three candidates \(\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\). Hence at least one voter in \(S_X\) must approve \(\geq3\) members of any EJR committee \(W\).  
  Voters 8–10 can reach three approvals only via two members of \(X\) plus \(z_1\). Voter 1 can reach three approvals via two members of \(X\) plus \(\{y_1,z_3\}\) (or via three members of \(X\)). Consequently every EJR committee must contain at least two members of \(X\), which already guarantees voter 1 at least two personally approved seats. Committees containing only a single member of \(X\) (even when augmented by both \(y_1\) and \(z_3\)) leave voters 8–10 with at most two approvals and therefore violate EJR.

- \(S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}\) (\(|S_Y|=4\geq 2\cdot2\)) shares exactly the three candidates \(\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}\). Hence at least one voter in \(S_Y\) must approve \(\geq2\) members of \(W\). This forces \(W\) to contain at least two candidates from \(\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\).

These two constraints together are satisfiable by many size-5 committees, but the second constraint leaves at most three seats that can be filled from voter 1’s ballot. Explicit constructions confirm the attainable values:

- Lower endpoint: \(W=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}\) satisfies both EJR conditions (voters 8–10 each obtain three seats; voters 4–7 each obtain two seats) while giving voter 1 exactly two personally approved members.  
- Upper endpoint: \(W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}\) likewise satisfies both conditions while giving voter 1 exactly three personally approved members.

No EJR committee can give voter 1 four (or five) seats: any selection of four candidates from \(\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_3\}\) leaves fewer than two seats for the representatives required by \(S_Y\). Hence the attainable range is exactly \([2,3]\).

H. min 2, max 3

6.text:
The main EJR constraints come from the two largest cohesive groups. The group \(S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}\) (\(|S_X|=6\)) is 3-cohesive on \(T=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\), so at least one voter in \(S_X\) must approve \(\ge3\) members of \(W\). The group \(S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}\) (\(|S_Y|=4\)) is 2-cohesive on \(T=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}\), so at least one voter in \(S_Y\) must approve \(\ge2\) members of \(W\).

Any feasible \(W\) must therefore contain at least two members of \(\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\) (otherwise, even after adding both \(y_1\) and \(z_3\), the maximum representation any voter in \(S_X\) can receive is only 2). This already guarantees voter 1 at least two personally approved seats. The same lower bound cannot be strengthened to three, because the explicit committee
\[
W=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}
\]
satisfies both EJR conditions above (voters 8–10 each obtain three seats; voters 4–5 each obtain two seats) while giving voter 1 exactly two approved representatives.

The upper bound is likewise three. Adding both \(y_1\) and \(z_3\) to any two \(x\)-candidates already consumes four seats; the single remaining seat cannot simultaneously give \(S_Y\) two approved representatives. Hence every committee that meets the two EJR conditions contains at most three members of voter 1’s ballot. The bound is tight: the committee
\[
W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}
\]
satisfies both EJR conditions and gives voter 1 exactly three approved representatives.

Consequently the attainable interval is exactly \([2,3]\).

PUBLIC RESPONSE: {H. min 2, max 3}

16.text:
The EJR axiom (with \(n=10\), \(k=5\)) requires that every \(\ell\)-cohesive coalition \(S\) (\(|S|\ge\ell\cdot2\) and \(|\cap_{i\in S}A_i|\ge\ell\)) has at least one member \(i\) with \(|A_i\cap W|\ge\ell\).

The coalition \(\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}\) is 3-cohesive on \(\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}\). The only voter inside this coalition who can possibly obtain three personal representatives when \(|W\cap X|=1\) is voter 1 (via \(y_1\) and \(z_3\)). The proper sub-coalition \(\{2,3,8,9,10\}\) (size 5) is nevertheless still 2-cohesive on the same three candidates; none of its members can reach two personal representatives when only a single \(x\)-candidate is elected. Hence every EJR committee must contain at least two members of \(X\), giving voter 1 a lower bound of two.

The coalition \(\{4,5,6,7\}\) is 2-cohesive on \(\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}\) and therefore forces \(W\) to contain at least two candidates from \(\{y_4,y_5,y_6,z_1,z_2\}\). This quota consumes two seats, leaving at most three seats that can intersect voter 1’s ballot. Explicit committees exist that attain exactly three (e.g., \(\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_4,y_5\}\)) and exactly two (e.g., \(\{x_1,x_2,y_1,z_3,z_1\}\)), both of which satisfy every cohesiveness constraint. Four or five seats for voter 1 always leaves the four-voter \(y\)-coalition short of its quota.

Consequently the attainable interval is exactly \([2,3]\).

public_text.11:
The EJR constraints are driven by two large cohesive groups: the 6-voter X-group (size ≥ 3·(n/k)) sharing {x1,x2,x3} and the 4-voter Y-group (size ≥ 2·(n/k)) sharing {y4,y5,y6}. The former forces |W ∩ X| ≥ 2 (otherwise no member of the group can reach 3 approved seats). The latter forces at least two Y-seats (or one Y-seat + z1).  

Any size-5 committee meeting both conditions therefore yields |W ∩ A1| ∈ {2,3}:
- |W ∩ X| = 2 + z1 + two Y-candidates satisfies both groups and gives voter 1 exactly two approvals.
- |W ∩ X| = 3 + two Y-candidates satisfies both groups and gives voter 1 exactly three approvals.

Adding y1 or z3 to reach four approvals for voter 1 necessarily displaces a needed Y-seat and violates the second constraint. Committees with |W ∩ X| = 1 (or 0) violate the first constraint. Hence the attainable interval is exactly [2,3] (choice H).  

This is corroborated by explicit realizing committees such as {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} and {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5}.

The EJR constraints are driven by two key coalitions: the 6-voter Sx group (ℓ=3, common approvals {x1,x2,x3}) and the 4-voter Sy group (ℓ=2, common approvals {y4,y5,y6}). Any valid W must therefore ensure that at least one member of Sx receives ≥3 approved seats (forcing |W ∩ X| ≥ 2, possibly augmented by z1 for voters 8–10) and at least one member of Sy receives ≥2 approved seats (forcing ≥2 seats from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}).

This immediately rules out |W ∩ A1| ≤ 1 (no member of Sx can then reach 3 approvals) and |W ∩ A1| ≥ 4 (any such committee necessarily under-represents Sy, e.g., {x1,x2,y1,z3,z1} gives Sy only one approved seat). Concrete realizing committees exist for both endpoints of the interval [2,3]:
- {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} yields exactly 2 for voter 1 while satisfying both EJR thresholds,
- {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5} yields exactly 3 for voter 1 while satisfying both thresholds.

Hence the attainable range is exactly 2–3 (choice H). All other reported intervals contain at least one explicit counter-example violating one of the two coalitions above.

The EJR condition requires that every ℓ-cohesive coalition \(S\) of size at least \(\ell\cdot(n/k)=\ell\cdot2\) has at least one member who approves at least \(\ell\) members of any valid committee \(W\).

The unique ℓ=3-cohesive coalition is the set of 6 voters {1,2,3,8,9,10} whose common intersection is exactly {x1,x2,x3}. Consequently at least one voter inside this coalition must approve ≥3 members of \(W\). Voters 8–10 can reach three approvals only via two X-candidates plus z1 (or three X-candidates). Voter 1 can reach three approvals via two X-candidates plus both y1 and z3. The only feasible realizations that also leave enough seats for every other coalition therefore require |W∩X|≥2; a single X-candidate leaves no way for any member of the coalition to reach three approvals. Hence every EJR committee already contains at least two candidates approved by voter 1, establishing the lower bound of 2.

The unique ℓ=2-cohesive coalition is the set of 4 voters {4,5,6,7} whose common intersection is {y4,y5,y6}. Consequently at least one member of this coalition must approve ≥2 members of \(W\), which forces W to contain at least two candidates from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. With |W|=5 this quota leaves at most three seats that can be filled from voter 1’s ballot. The only way to reach four approvals for voter 1 would be to place three X-candidates together with both y1 and z3, leaving zero seats for the Y-coalition quota—an immediate EJR violation. Hence the attainable numbers never exceed three.

Explicit realizing committees are
- {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1} (|W∩A1|=2) and
- {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5} (|W∩A1|=3).

Both satisfy EJR for every cohesive coalition. Consequently the attainable interval is exactly [2,3].
